title: Derived mate criterion from compatible injective resolutions
statement: Let A,B,C,D be abelian categories with ordinary unbounded derived categories and K-injective resolutions in B and D. Let L ⊣ R and L′ ⊣ R′ be additive adjunctions, with exact L and L′. Let G : A → C and H : B → D be exact additive functors and s : G ⋙ L′ ≅ L ⋙ H. Assume the ordinary mate of s.hom is invertible. Assume that for each K-injective complex I of B, each quasi-isomorphic K-injective resolution j : H(I) → J in D stays a quasi-isomorphism under R′. Then the mate for the derived adjunctions of the inverse of the derived square of s.symm is invertible.

source.place: Tags 03EK and 0D6E; already proved generic subargument of blueprint sk-thm-purity-transport Step 10, moved from the assigned module for compile performance.

proof.text: For a K-injective I choose a K-injective resolution of H(I). The resolution hypothesis makes the derived unit for R′ at H(I) invertible; the derived unit for R at I is invertible because I is K-injective. The existing derived-mate factorization identifies the component, after multiplying by these units and canonical comparison isomorphisms, with the derived image of the ordinary mate. This is invertible. Cancel the units and comparisons. Every derived object is isomorphic to the image of a K-injective complex, so naturality transfers componentwise invertibility to every object. The derived square construction sends symmetry to inversion, giving the displayed orientation.
